clue.text: Dwarf, clutching ten cents, is quite undeveloped

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing something at its first, most basic stage; the answer is the noun for such a beginning

indicators.note: the dwarf holds the coin in its grasp, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a runt is an undersized creature, a dwarf
a dime is the American ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A stunted little man pockets a dime and is called immature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' reads as a verb but is the noun for an undersized creature. The answer is a noun for a first, undeveloped stage, defined loosely by an adjectival phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A first principle or embryonic organ is at the earliest stage of growth, not yet formed.

clue.text: Statement concerning wine

parts.note: re means concerning, about
port is a fortified wine

explanation.definitionFit: An account, a spoken or written statement of events.

clue.text: Follower of La Pompadour

parts.note: Madame de Pompadour is credited with the remark that after her would come the flood; the follower is that flood

explanation.walkthrough: The follower is not a lover but what she said would come after her: 'Après nous, le déluge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A great flood, the catastrophe she said would follow her.

clue.text: She's a crazy soul

parts.note: mad means crazy
âme is French for soul

explanation.surface: A woman with a deranged spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman, so a way to refer to her.

clue.text: Occasional timely contrasts

definitions.meaning: happening at intervals, from time to time
two words for times that contrast, the present and the past

explanation.surface: Contrasts that crop up only once in a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sometimes, and its two halves are opposed times, present against past.

clue.text: It's grown into a double-bill, first-class turn !

indicators.note: double asks for the word for bill to be written twice in a row

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the first-class mark from back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the 1 is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Something has grown into a first-rate double-bill entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives ACAC; 'turn' reverses AI (A1, first-class) to IA. 'into a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The wattle tree is a plant, something cultivated and grown.

clue.text: Director does his turn as payee

indicators.note: doing a turn means performing a reshuffle, so the director's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director performs his act to get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does his turn' signals the anagram of DIRECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One owed money is the party who receives payment.

clue.text: The old Italian heel is now the toe

definitions.text: The old Italian heel is now the toe

parts.words: The old Italian heel is now the toe
parts.note: the Romans gave this name to the heel of Italy's boot; it later moved to the toe region

explanation.walkthrough: In Roman times the name belonged to the south-eastern heel (modern Apulia); in the Middle Ages it passed to the south-western toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of southern Italy, now the toe of the boot, whose ancient namesake was the heel.

clue.text: Such a warning from the Capitol

definitions.text: Such a warning from the Capitol

parts.words: Such a warning from the Capitol
parts.note: the sacred geese on the Capitol cackled and woke Rome's defenders against the Gauls

explanation.walkthrough: In 390 BC Juno's geese on the Capitoline Hill raised the alarm; the answer means goose-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose-like alarm, as raised by the Roman birds.

clue.text: That false man of Sussex

parts.note: points to the famous fossil hoax, a skull 'discovered' in a Sussex gravel pit and long passed off as an early human

explanation.walkthrough: The skull found in Sussex in 1912 was exposed as a forgery in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The bogus early human from that county was named after the village where the bones were found.

clue.text: Hades as a home for the ancients ?

parts.note: Hades, the underworld, is hell

explanation.surface: Was the underworld where the ancients lived?
explanation.walkthrough: The ancients are the classical Greeks, and this was their own name for their country.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek name for Greece, homeland of the classical peoples.

clue.text: The boy intended to construct a sound unit

indicators.note: sound tells us the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the boy is Reggie, and intended is meant: said together, Reggie meant

explanation.surface: A lad meant to build a solid military formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' does double duty in the surface as 'solid'; spoken, 'Reggie meant' gives the answer. 'to construct a' is link text.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a military unit, a body of soldiers under a colonel.

clue.text: Actor and playwright has lost his shaggy dog apparently !

definitions.text: Actor and playwright has lost his shaggy dog apparently !

parts.words: Actor and playwright has lost his shaggy dog apparently !
parts.note: the eighteenth-century actor and dramatist's first name, Colley, sounds like the collie, a shaggy sheepdog; drop it and the surname is left

explanation.walkthrough: Colley Cibber was an English actor-manager, playwright and Poet Laureate; his first name puns on the collie.
explanation.definitionFit: Colley Cibber wrote comedies and acted at Drury Lane, so the surname alone names this stage figure.

clue.text: Roasting it for a change should be stimulating

definitions.note: describes the person the answer names, one whose role is to stir things up

indicators.note: for a change says these letters are altered into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cooking it differently ought to be exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' signals the anagram of ROASTING IT.
explanation.definitionFit: One who provokes or incites action, a person whose job is to rouse others.

clue.text: Having the voice of fifty

parts.note: in Homer's Iliad the Greek herald Stentor shouted as loud as fifty men together

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective comes from Stentor, the herald in the Iliad whose voice matched fifty men's.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a booming, extremely loud voice, after Homer's herald.

clue.text: Meeting in the outhouse made things easy

indicators.note: in places the meeting within the outhouse

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
a moot is an assembly, a meeting

explanation.surface: Getting together in a garden shed eased matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' is the old word for an assembly, as in a moot court; the outhouse is a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased the way, removed difficulties.

clue.text: He inevitably makes a stir

parts.note: a person whose business is to stir up unrest, or a machine paddle that stirs

explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker who rouses discontent, or a mixing device in a washing machine.

clue.text: Let's get opposite to each other for a talk

definitions.meaning: a statement turned around is its opposite

explanation.surface: Let's sit face to face and chat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means the opposite; as a verb it means to hold a conversation.

clue.text: A dear little French flower

definitions.meaning: French for a sweet little darling girl, the feminine diminutive of mignon
a fragrant garden plant, Reseda odorata

explanation.definitionFit: The French endearment for a little darling also names the sweet-scented reseda plant.

clue.text: Tailor's son was a painter

parts.note: the Florentine painter was called 'del Sarto', of the tailor, after his father's trade

explanation.walkthrough: Andrea del Sarto, the Renaissance painter, took his name from his father, a tailor (sarto).
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the Renaissance painter Andrea del Sarto.

clue.text: Time for 23 ?

definitions.meaning: points to the answer at 23 across, the Muses' source on Helicon, which is a water source of this kind

explanation.surface: When is the right season for the Muses' haunt?
explanation.definitionFit: The season after winter, and a natural fountain of water like Helicon's.

clue.text: This little hound was a great voyager

definitions.meaning: HMS ship of that name carried Darwin round the world

explanation.definitionFit: A small scent-hound, and the survey ship that carried Darwin on his voyage.

clue.text: Time for a stretch at the piano

definitions.meaning: in the church calendar, the eight days following a feast
the span of eight notes a pianist's hand reaches across

explanation.surface: How long does a pianist rest between pieces?
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on eight: an eight-day festival period and an eight-note interval on the keyboard.

clue.text: Where the Muses got pep again, presumably

indicators.note: presumably hints that the letters were put together in some other order than written

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Muses went somewhere to be revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presumably' signals the anagram of PEP AGAIN; 'got' is a link. Aganippe was a spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred spring on Helicon where the nine goddesses of the arts drank for inspiration.

clue.text: The malicious only cause broken hearts

indicators.note: broken means the word hearts is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Spiteful people do nothing but break hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful, hostile people are those who feel enmity.

clue.text: Beginning with something sharp about the pictures

indicators.note: about means the sharp thing goes round the pictures

parts.note: a sting is a sharp prick or pain
art is pictures, paintings in general

explanation.surface: Opening with a pointed remark about the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pictures' looks like the cinema but means paintings in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Commencing, setting off on something.

clue.text: Doorway exercise forbidden to scapegrace Victorians

definitions.text: Doorway exercise forbidden to scapegrace Victorians

parts.words: Doorway exercise forbidden to scapegrace Victorians
parts.note: recalls the Victorian father's dismissal of a disgraced son: never again cast your shadow across my door

explanation.walkthrough: The stock melodrama line is 'Never darken my door again', said to a scapegrace (a rogue) being disowned.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a shadow on, make dim, as the banished son must never do to the family door.

clue.text: Eternal music-maker ?

definitions.meaning: the eternal love affair of three people is a stock phrase
a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into a three-sided shape and struck

explanation.definitionFit: Both the classic love affair among three and the orchestral instrument take this three-sided name.
